data.title: Show HN: Somo – a human friendly alternative to netstat
data.author: hollow64
data.article_summary: Somo是一款用于Linux系统上监控socket和端口的工具，作为netstat的更人性化替代品。它具有直观的表格视图，支持多种过滤选项，并能够交互式地终止进程。安装方式有通过Debian的.deb包或使用cargo进行安装，运行时通常需要sudo权限。Somo提供多种过滤标志，如按协议、端口、IP、程序、PID等进行筛选，还支持结合过滤和终止进程操作。该工具旨在简化网络连接和端口的管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工具的可用性及功能优化，尤其是关于表格模式的开启/关闭和在不同操作系统中的适用性。

不同观点：
• [ale42] 认为表格模式（尤其是横线）占据了终端的太多空间，询问是否可以禁用该模式，以提高在多个连接打开时的显示效率。
• [nubb] 表示已经习惯使用 `netstat -pna` 命令，认为使用其他工具会不适应，强调个人习惯和对新工具的抵触。
• [mrweasel] 支持工具的实用性，认为该工具解决了其在大多数情况下记不住 `netstat` 参数的问题，尤其在90%的使用场景中都能满足需求。
• [basemi] 提供了另一个命令 `ss` 作为替代选项，并提供了相关文档链接（https://linux.die.net/man/8/ss），建议讨论者参考。
• [at0mic22] 指出该工具在Mac OS上不可用，原因是 `procfs` 不支持，强调操作系统兼容性的问题。

补充讨论：
• 用户对工具的个性化需求存在差异，例如 [ale42] 希望有更多自定义选项（如关闭表格模式）。
• 不同用户对新工具的态度存在分歧，[nubb] 更倾向于坚持使用熟悉的 `netstat`，而 [mrweasel] 则对新工具持欢迎态度。
• 操作系统兼容性问题也被提出作为工具使用的一个限制，[at0mic22] 特别指出了Mac OS上的限制。

争议焦点：
• 工具的自定义选项是否足够灵活，尤其是针对界面显示（如表格模式）的优化需求。
• 新工具与传统命令（如 `netstat`）之间的取舍，部分用户认为新工具更好用，而部分用户则依赖旧工具的习惯。

A human-friendly alternative to netstat for socket and port monitoring on Linux.
✨ Features:
pleasing to the eye thanks to a nice table-view
filterable (see filter-options below)
interactive killing of processes
from
netstat -tulpn
to
somo -l
(almost half the characters, can you believe it?)
⬇️ Installation:
Option 1 - Debian:
If you use a Debian OS go to
releases
and download the latest .deb release.
Option 2 - From crates.io:
cargo install somo
Most of the time you will want to run this in
sudo
mode to see all processes and ports. By default, this is not possible when installed via cargo. But you can create a symlink so the binary can be run as root:
sudo ln -s
~
/.cargo/bin/somo /usr/local/bin/somo
sudo somo
#
this works now
🏃‍♀️ Running somo:
To run somo just type:
sudo somo
Filtering:
You can use the following flags to filter based on different attributes:
filter flag
description
value
--proto
filter by either TCP or UDP
tcp
or
udp
--port, -p
filter by a local port
port number, e.g
5433
--remote-port
filter by a remote port
port number, e.g
443
--ip
filter by a remote IP
IP address e.g
0.0.0.0
--program
filter by a client program
program name e.g
chrome
--pid, -p
filter by a PID
PID number, e.g
10000
--open, -o
filter by open connections
-
--listen, -l
filter by open connections
-
--exclude-ipv6
don't list IPv6 connections
-
Process killing:
With the
--kill, -k
flag you can choose to kill a process after inspecting the connections using an interactive selection option.
You can of course also apply filters and the kill-flag at the same time:
somo --program postgres -k

A human-friendly alternative to netstat for socket and port monitoring on Linux.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Rust库"glowstick"，它通过类型系统跟踪张量形状，使处理张量更加安全、简单和有趣。该库支持渐进类型，允许表达和处理动态维度，并提供了人性化的错误信息。主要功能包括：通过类型表达张量形状，支持所有ONNX操作，以及手动检查类型级别的形状。文章还展示了如何使用"glowstick"进行矩阵乘法、卷积、张量变形、广播加法等操作，并提供了与Rust机器学习框架（如candle和Burn）集成的示例。需注意，该项目尚未发布1.0版本，可能会有重大变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Barry Jay的形状理论及其在多维数组处理中的应用，特别是在FiSh语言中的静态形状检查和循环优化，以及与现代编译器优化（如Rust）的比较。

不同观点：
• [srean] 认为Barry Jay的形状理论在FiSh语言中对多维数组的形状处理和静态类型检查非常有效，并且在循环优化中起到了重要作用。他提供了相关文献链接以支持其观点。
• [raphaelty] 对[srean]的观点表示赞同，并进一步提出希望类似的功能可以集成到编译器中，特别是与ML和Rust的结合使用表示赞赏。
• [bee_rider] 对形状理论在多维数组优化中的独特性提出疑问，指出像Eigen这样的库在矩阵运算优化（如4x4矩阵求逆）中也有类似的技巧，如循环展开等。他还建议可以尝试使用现代优化编译器（如Rust的不同优化级别）来看看是否能达到类似的效果。

补充讨论：
• [bee_rider] 提出一个实际问题，即在现代编译器已经具备较强优化能力的背景下，是否仍有必要专门使用形状理论来进行优化。他建议通过实验比较Rust编译器的自动优化效果与形状理论的优化效果。
• 争议的焦点在于形状理论在当前技术环境下的独特价值和必要性。一方面，[srean]和[raphaelty]强调其在特定语言和应用中的重要性和潜在优势；另一方面，[bee_rider]则质疑其在现代优化编译器面前的不可替代性。

总结：讨论围绕Barry Jay的形状理论在多维数组处理和优化中的应用展开，涉及其在FiSh语言中的实现和与现代编译器优化技术的比较。不同的观点集中在形状理论的独特价值和在当前技术环境下的应用前景上。

data.title: Algovivo an energy-based formulation for soft-bodied virtual creatures
data.author: tzury
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：潜在能量最小化与目标导向行为之间的关系，以及能量函数在模拟系统中的应用

不同观点：
• [abeppu] 对“潜在能量最小化是基本的目标导向行为”这一观点感到困惑。他认为，无生命物体（如滚动的足球）的势能最小化并非目标导向行为，这与有目标的系统（如动物行走）不同。他指出，势能最小化可能只是实现目标的策略之一，而不是目标本身，例如猛禽利用高度势能快速俯冲捕食。此外，他提醒需要区分物理能量的模拟与能量作为系统控制或影响的隐喻性表达。

• [Bjartr] 提到一个名为 Soda Play / Soda Constructor 的旧模拟游戏，这个游戏可能与讨论的框架有相似之处，暗示这种能量最小化和目标导向的讨论可能在早期的模拟中已有体现。

• [monster_truck] 对模拟系统的技术细节发表评论，指出在操作过程中可以发现系统中的某些状态（如抓住中间点）可能导致锁定状态，这是一种技术实现上的观察。

• [bcoates] 提出关于模拟系统行为的具体问题，询问为什么在启动“大脑”时，小物体（模拟系统中的对象）会向前移动，这似乎是在寻求对系统行为的具体解释。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于势能最小化是否可以直接等同于目标导向行为。 [abeppu] 认为这两者有本质区别，而其他评论者主要关注模拟系统的实现和技术细节。
• [abeppu] 还提醒注意能量函数在不同情境下的不同含义，强调需要区分物理模拟和隐喻性表达。

通过这些观点，可以看出讨论的核心在于如何理解和应用势能最小化与目标导向行为之间的关系，以及在模拟系统中如何准确地建模和解释这些行为。

data.title: Maypole Dance of Braid Like Groups (2009)
data.author: srean
data.article_summary:
本文描述了作者在五一节派对上观察到的花柱舞，并从数学角度用辫群理论对其进行分析。花柱舞中，舞者手持彩带围绕花柱跳舞，彩带形成类似辫子的图案。作者将此与辫群（braid group）联系起来，辫群是由一系列弦按特定规则交织而成，且不能打结。传统的辫群是由两个杆之间的弦构成，而花柱舞的辫子是在圆柱表面形成，弦连接两个圆，且不能穿过花柱轴心。

作者提出了一种“花柱辫群”的概念，指出其不同于传统辫群。为了描述这种群，需要增加新的生成元和关系。具体来说，除了原有的生成元，还需加入一个表示整体旋转的新生成元，以完整描述花柱舞的辫子图案。

主要讨论点：Maypole群、编织与织布的关系以及编织群（braid group）在物理学中的应用。

不同观点：
• [mathgradthrow] 认为Maypole群确实是编织群（braid group）的一个子群，提出可以通过将杆本身作为最右边的线股来实现这一点。这表明他从数学结构的角度来理解Maypole群与编织群的关系。

• [srean] 表达了对近期关于编织和织布话题的兴趣，并指出相比之下，织布更容易理解。他还提到有意购买多轴织布机，但抱怨价格昂贵。他的观点更多是从实际操作和个人兴趣出发，关注编织和织布的实践性。

• [jiggawatts] 指出编织群与理论物理中基本粒子代数之间存在有趣的相似性，虽然他认为这种联系可能是代数形式主义的产物，但仍然觉得这种联系不容忽视。他的观点侧重于编织群在物理学中的潜在应用和理论意义。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了不同的领域，包括数学（编织群和子群问题）、编织/织布的实际操作（如多轴织布机）以及物理学（编织群与基本粒子理论的联系）。
• [jiggawatts] 的评论引入了关于编织群在理论物理中应用的争议，即这种联系是否仅仅是代数形式上的巧合，还是具有更深层次的物理意义。
• [srean] 的评论还暗示了编织和织布作为手工艺术的吸引力以及实践中的经济障碍（如设备昂贵）。

这些观点展示了编织群和相关概念在数学、物理学以及手工艺术中的多重意义和应用。

Over the weekend I attended a
May Day
party thrown by one of my colleagues.
During the party they had a traditional
maypole dance
. An example of a maypole dance is shown at left. A maypole is a tall pole with colorful ribbons attached to the top that are fanned out in a cone shape. The dancers hold the ribbons and dance according to the rules called by the party’s host (like a square dance). Some walk clockwise and others walk counterclockwise. When one dancer encounters another she goes under the other’s ribbon or lets the other dancer go under hers (according to the rules of the dance).  As this is happening the ribbons wind around the pole, making a decorative pattern, such as those shown below.
Having just taught the last day of my
knot theory
class the day before the party I couldn’t help but look at the maypole with a mathematical eye.
One of the topics in my knot theory course was the
(Artin) braid group
. A
braid
is a collection of
strings hanging from a rod, wound around each other, and attached to another rod below so that each string is always going downward (as in the picture below). Note that there can be no knotting in the strands because that would require the strings to move upward temporarily.
This is a bona fide
group
. The group operation is concatenation—i.e, to mutiply two braids, attach the second braid to the bottom of the first. 本文描述了作者在五一节派对上观察到的花柱舞，并从数学角度用辫群理论对其进行分析。花柱舞中，舞者手持彩带围绕花柱跳舞，彩带形成类似辫子的图案。作者将此与辫群（braid group）联系起来，辫群是由一系列弦按特定规则交织而成，且不能打结。传统的辫群是由两个杆之间的弦构成，而花柱舞的辫子是在圆柱表面形成，弦连接两个圆，且不能穿过花柱轴心。

作者提出了一种“花柱辫群”的概念，指出其不同于传统辫群。为了描述这种群，需要增加新的生成元和关系。具体来说，除了原有的生成元，还需加入一个表示整体旋转的新生成元，以完整描述花柱舞的辫子图案。

data.title: A man rebuilding the last Inca rope bridge
data.author: kaonwarb
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了秘鲁安第斯山脉中的一座独特的手工编织绳索桥——Q'eswachaka桥。这座桥由草和纤维制成，悬挂在60英尺高的湍急河流上方，每年由当地社区重建。Victoriano Arizapana是唯一掌握这一500多年传统技艺的人，他的家族自印加帝国时期以来一直领导着这座桥的修建。Q'eswachaka桥是现存唯一的印加绳索桥，象征着古老传统的延续。文章还提到记者Eliot Stein的书《Custodians of Wonder》，该书讲述了全球范围内正在消失的古老传统和守护这些传统的最后守护者。Stein通过访问像Victoriano这样的守护者，记录下这些珍贵的文化遗产。

Keshwa chaca, among the last handwoven Incan bridges, crosses Apurimac Canyon in Peru.

Every year, high in the
Andes Mountains in Peru, a man builds a bridge. The bridge is strong enough to hold the weight of more than one hundred men. But it isn’t made of iron or steel. It’s made of grasses and fibers. It hangs 60 feet above a thundering river.
And the man is not a construction worker or a structural engineer—but he is the only person on earth who knows how to build this particular bridge. That man’s name is Victoriano Arizapana, and he is the heir to a tradition that is over 500 years old.
The Inca Empire built elaborate rope bridges to cross vast chasms in the Andes.
Today, only one of those bridges remains: the Q’eswachaka. Every single year since the Inca Empire, Victoriano’s family has led the local community in cutting the bridge down and reweaving it from scratch.
I’m Dylan Thuras, and this is Atlas Obscura.
This is an edited transcript of the
Atlas Obscura Podcast
: a celebration of the world’s strange, incredible, and wondrous places. Find the show on
Apple Podcasts
,
Spotify
, and all major podcast apps.
The view from the Q’eswachaka woven suspension bridge.
Dylan Thuras / Atlas Obscura
Dylan Thuras:
We often hear about the first person to do something—an inventor, a pioneer. It’s rarer to hear about the last person to carry on a tradition. Today, I’m talking with Eliot Stein. He’s a journalist for the BBC, and he traveled across the world reporting on rare and ancient practices and talking to the final stewards keeping these traditions alive.
It includes a visit to one of the greatest places that I have ever been in my life—a place sometimes called the Last Incan Bridge, but better known as the Q’eswachaka. Eliot chronicled this in his book,
Custodians of Wonder: Ancient Customs, Profound Traditions, and the Last People Keeping Them Alive
.
Hey, Eliot. Thanks for joining.
Eliot Stein:
Hey, thanks so much for having me.
Dylan:
Yeah. Your book is called
Custodians of Wonder
. What drew you to this subject matter?
Eliot:
I had this chance encounter 20 years ago that effectively changed my life. I was leading tours in Italy, and off an island near Venice called Burano, I came across this 90-year-old woman who, for whatever reason, took an interest in me and led me into her home.
She was blind, and she asked me to take a look at her life’s work, which was hung up on the wall. It was lace, but it was very clear to me that I’d never seen anything like this. It looked sort of like stitched seafoam or embroidered spider webs. I was asking her to tell me about this, and it quickly became clear to me that it wasn’t just beautiful, but for 300 years, this lace that was only made on this one small island was one of the most coveted items in the Western world.
It was the boast of royalty, the height of fashion, the target of international smuggling—but more than anything, for this rather anonymous group of women, it was their life. It was their pride. It was something that means something to them.
This kind of awakened in me this sympathy, this reverence for these final custodians who—the woman’s name was Anna—all she wanted was for visitors like myself to understand what makes this island so special; and that was really what drew me to this as a way to kind of quietly cast a light on people who are humble, are anonymous, but have given something beautiful to the world.
Dylan:
It’s a great book, and I think we’re going to be covering a number of stories from this book on the show over time. But today, we’re going to talk about one of my favorite places that I’ve ever been, one of the coolest people I’ve ever met. We’re going to be talking about Victoriano Arizapana, the bridgekeeper, and the Q’eswachaka, sometimes called the Last Incan Bridge.
But to understand the story, I think you really have to start with the Incan Empire. It’s one of the world’s most fascinating civilizations. It develops in basically relative isolation and becomes one of the largest empires in the world at the time.
So maybe we could start by talking about how that happened.
Eliot:
The way that they did that was through this incredible road system called the Qhapaq Ñan, which means the Royal Road in Quechua. And the Royal Road was rivaled only in history by the Roman road system.
And at its height, it spanned 40,000 kilometers, which is roughly the circumference of the globe. It was an incredible feat of engineering, and compared to the Roman road system—which traversed a relatively uniform topography—the Inca Empire went from the snow-capped peaks of the Andes down to the steamy basin of the Amazon.
And to do that, these people who didn’t have wheels, mortar, written language, they bore massive tunnels through the mountains. They paved stones so that they were as clear

data.title: Apple introduces a universal design across platforms
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 苹果公司于2025年6月9日发布了全新软件设计，涵盖iOS 26、iPadOS 26、macOS Tahoe 26、watchOS 26和tvOS 26。该设计引入了名为“Liquid Glass”的新材料，具有透明、反射和折射特性，能根据内容和环境动态变化，增强用户对内容的关注。新设计在保持各平台独特性的同时，带来了更高的一致性与活力，优化了控件、导航、应用图标、小部件等元素。Liquid Glass材料适用于按钮、滑块、文本和媒体控制等小元素，以及标签栏和侧边栏等大元素，并在系统界面如锁屏、主屏幕和控制中心等处展现出更生动的体验。更新后的设计在相机、照片、Safari、FaceTime等应用中提供了更直观、易用的操作体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple新推出的"Liquid Glass"设计及其影响，尤其是在用户界面（UI）设计、可访问性（accessibility）、以及与以往设计风格的比较方面。

不同观点：
• **可访问性问题**（dimal, stalco, socalgal2）：dimal（自闭症患者）指出，透明图层和模糊效果会导致文本难以辨认，可能对包括自闭症患者在内的很多人造成困扰。stalco和socalgal2也提到新设计对眼睛不友好，特别是对年长或视力不佳的用户。他们呼吁提供关闭或自定义这些效果的选项。

• **与以往设计风格的比较**（Someone1234, ksec, kej）：Someone1234怀念拟物设计（skeuomorphic design）的时代，认为那时的设计更注重可用性和教学性。ksec认为当前的设计重复了Windows Vista和iOS 7的错误，而kej则将其与微软的Metro设计相比较，质疑Apple是否会重蹈覆辙。

• **设计的美学与实用性**（plainOldText, captainmuon, sarreph, pentagrama）：plainOldText和pentagrama认为新设计视觉上过于复杂，可能导致用户疲劳。captainmuon则持积极态度，认为新设计利用了现代显示技术，可以带来更具物理质感的UI。sarreph认为Liquid Glass是设计进化的一部分，代表了一种新的“新拟物风格”（Neo Skeuomorphism），并预测这种风格会逐渐被广泛接受。

• **技术实现与市场策略**（kylehotchkiss, nharada, gherkinnn）：kylehotchkiss赞赏Apple在设计上的投资，但指出一些应用（如Slack）可能会显得格格不入。nharada推测透明设计可能是为未来的AR界面做准备。gherkinnn引用了一篇博客，认为Apple的设计趋势早在多年前就有预测，并表达了对玻璃UI的喜爱。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：新设计的可访问性和视觉复杂性是主要争议点。许多用户担心透明效果和低对比度会降低可用性，特别是对有特殊需求的用户。同时，一些用户质疑Apple是否过于追求视觉效果而忽视了实用性。

• **解决方案**：大多数用户希望Apple提供关闭或自定义这些效果的选项，以满足不同用户的需求。有些人则认为Apple可能会在后续更新中调整设计，解决当前的问题。

• **历史趋势与未来展望**：评论中多次提到iOS 7和Vista的设计失误，用户担心历史重演。同时，也有观点认为Apple可能在为未来的AR技术做准备，新设计可能是统一多平台设计语言的一部分。

PRESS RELEASE
June 9, 2025
Apple introduces a delightful and elegant new software design
A universal design across platforms brings more focus to content and a new level of vitality while maintaining the familiarity of Apple’s software
The new design extends across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26 to establish even more harmony while maintaining the distinct qualities that make each platform unique.
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA
Apple today previewed a beautiful new software design that makes apps and system experiences more expressive and delightful while being instantly familiar. It’s crafted with a new material called Liquid Glass. This translucent material reflects and refracts its surroundings, while dynamically transforming to help bring greater focus to content, delivering a new level of vitality across controls, navigation, app icons, widgets, and more. For the very first time, the new design extends across platforms — iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26
1
— to establish even more harmony while maintaining the distinct qualities that make each unique.
“At Apple, we’ve always believed in the deep integration of hardware and software that makes interacting with technology intuitive, beautiful, and delightful,” said Alan Dye, Apple’s vice president of Human Interface Design. “This is our broadest software design update ever. Meticulously crafted by rethinking the fundamental elements that make up our software, the new design features an entirely new material called Liquid Glass. It combines the optical qualities of glass with a fluidity only Apple can achieve, as it transforms depending on your content or context. It lays the foundation for new experiences in the future and, ultimately, it makes even the simplest of interactions more fun and magical.”
The new material, Liquid Glass, combines the optical qualities of glass with a fluidity only Apple can achieve, transforming depending on the content or context.
Introducing Liquid Glass: A New and Expressive Material
Inspired by the depth and dimensionality of visionOS, the new design takes advantage of Apple’s powerful advances in hardware, silicon, and graphics technologies. The new material, Liquid Glass, is translucent and behaves like glass in the real world. Its color is informed by surrounding content and intelligently adapts between light and dark environments. Born out of a close collaboration between the design and engineering teams, Liquid Glass uses real-time rendering and dynamically reacts to movement with specular highlights. This creates a lively experience that makes using iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Apple TV even more delightful.
This gorgeous new material extends from the smallest elements users interact with every day — like buttons, switches, sliders, text, and media controls — to larger elements, including tab bars and sidebars for navigating apps. It also shines in system experiences, such as the Lock Screen, Home Screen, notifications, Control Center, and more.
The new material, Liquid Glass, combines the optical qualities of glass with a fluidity only Apple can achieve, as it transforms depending on the content or context.
Updated App Designs
Driven by the goal of bringing greater focus to content that’s instantly familiar, Apple’s design team considered every aspect of Apple’s platforms to identify improvements that could be made across the board.
Controls, toolbars, and navigation within apps have been redesigned. Previously configured for rectangular displays, they now fit perfectly concentric with the rounded corners of modern hardware and app windows — establishing greater harmony between hardware, software, and content. Controls are crafted out of Liquid Glass and act as a distinct functional layer that sits above apps. They give way to content and dynamically morph as users need more options or move between different parts of an app. And with thoughtful groupings, it’s easier for users to find the controls they need.
Controls and navigation across apps are crafted from Liquid Glass, and fluidly transform to bring more focus to a user’s content.
Tab bars and sidebars have been redesigned with the same approach. In iOS 26, when users scroll, tab bars shrink to bring focus to the content while keeping navigation instantly accessible. The moment users scroll back up, tab bars fluidly expand. In iPadOS and macOS, updated sidebars make apps like Apple TV even more immersive. They refract the content behind them — while reflecting content and the user’s wallpaper from around them — which ensures users always have a sense of their context.
These updated design elements apply across fresh new experiences in apps such as Camera, Photos, Safari, FaceTime, Apple Music, Apple News, and Apple Podcasts.

• **与以往设计风格的比较**（Someone1234, ksec, kej）：Someone1234怀念拟物设计（skeuomorphic design）的时代，认为那时的设计更注重可用性和教学性。ksec认为当前的设计重复了Windows Vista和iOS 7的错误，而kej则将其与微软的Metro设计相比较，质疑Apple是否会重蹈覆辙。

• **设计的美学与实用性**（plainOldText, captainmuon, sarreph, pentagrama）：plainOldText和pentagrama认为新设计视觉上过于复杂，可能导致用户疲劳。captainmuon则持积极态度，认为新设计利用了现代显示技术，可以带来更具物理质感的UI。sarreph认为Liquid Glass是设计进化的一部分，代表了一种新的“新拟物风格”（Neo Skeuomorphism），并预测这种风格会逐渐被广泛接受。

• **技术实现与市场策略**（kylehotchkiss, nharada, gherkinnn）：kylehotchkiss赞赏Apple在设计上的投资，但指出一些应用（如Slack）可能会显得格格不入。nharada推测透明设计可能是为未来的AR界面做准备。gherkinnn引用了一篇博客，认为Apple的设计趋势早在多年前就有预测，并表达了对玻璃UI的喜爱。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：新设计的可访问性和视觉复杂性是主要争议点。许多用户担心透明效果和低对比度会降低可用性，特别是对有特殊需求的用户。同时，一些用户质疑Apple是否过于追求视觉效果而忽视了实用性。

• **解决方案**：大多数用户希望Apple提供关闭或自定义这些效果的选项，以满足不同用户的需求。有些人则认为Apple可能会在后续更新中调整设计，解决当前的问题。

• **历史趋势与未来展望**：评论中多次提到iOS 7和Vista的设计失误，用户担心历史重演。同时，也有观点认为Apple可能在为未来的AR技术做准备，新设计可能是统一多平台设计语言的一部分。

data.title: Potential and Limitation of High-Frequency Cores and Caches (2024)
data.author: matt_d
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了低温半导体计算和超导体电子学作为传统半导体器件的替代技术，分析了它们在高性能和低功耗计算方面的潜力。低温半导体器件在低温下运行可减少漏电流并提高电子迁移率，而超导体在接近绝对零度的条件下实现无电阻电子流动，提供超低功耗和高速度的计算能力。文章通过gem5模拟器对有序和无序执行核心的性能进行建模和分析，使用NPB、SPEC CPU2006和GAPBS等工作负载评估其性能。结果显示这些技术具有显著的速度提升潜力，但也面临缓存带宽等限制。文章为未来在这些技术上的研究奠定了基础。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IBM在超导体组件与常规CMOS互连及I/O性能上的假设是否合理

不同观点：
• Bob1029对文章中未考虑SERDES电路的影响表示调侃和质疑。他认为，假设超导体组件与室温CMOS组件之间的互连不变是不现实的，尤其是在高速数据传输的场景下。I/O性能（即数据从A点到B点的传输能力）通常是系统设计中的难点，而不是CPU的处理能力。
• 另一隐含观点是，IBM可能在推动实际应用的极限，尤其是在每个核心达到5.5GHz的基础时钟频率时。在这种情况下，核心处理能力不再是瓶颈，而I/O和周边组件的能力成为限制因素。

补充讨论：
• Bob1029提到软件可能是整个系统中的薄弱环节，尤其是在非一致性内存访问（NUMA）架构中，如果软件没有正确处理这些架构特性，系统的整体性能和效率会受到严重影响。这也表明，硬件性能的提升可能被软件层面的问题所抵消。
• 讨论中还涉及到抽象层次的问题，指出过多的软件抽象可能导致开发者在处理底层硬件特性时犯错，从而影响系统性能。

争议焦点：IBM在研究中对互连和I/O性能的假设是否过于简化，忽视了实际工程中的挑战。

Local Download

Presentation Download
This paper explores the potential of cryogenic semiconductor computing and superconductor electronics as promising alternatives to traditional semiconductor devices. As semiconductor devices face challenges such as increased leakage currents and reduced performance at higher temperatures, these novel technologies offer high performance and low power computation. Conventional semiconductor electronics operating at cryogenic temperatures (below -150°C or 123.15 K) can benefit from reduced leakage currents and improved electron mobility. On the other hand, superconductor electronics, operating below 10 K, allow electrons to flow without resistance, offering the potential for ultra-low-power, high-speed computation. This study presents a comprehensive performance modeling and analysis of these technologies and provides insights into their potential benefits and limitations. We implement models of in-order and out-of-order cores operating at high clock frequencies associated with superconductor electronics and cryogenic semiconductor computing in gem5. We evaluate the performance of these components using workloads representative of real-world applications like NPB, SPEC CPU2006, and GAPBS. Our results show the potential speedups achievable by these components and the limitations posed by cache bandwidth. This work provides valuable insights into the performance implications and design trade-offs associated with cryogenic and superconductor technologies, laying the foundation for future research in this field using gem5.

data.title: Frederick Forsyth has died
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 英国著名作家弗雷德里克·福赛斯（Frederick Forsyth）于86岁去世。他曾是记者和MI6情报人员，将真实经历融入惊悚小说创作，代表作包括《豺狼的日子》、《敖德萨档案》和《战争的狗》。他的小说以详实的调查和扣人心弦的情节著称，全球销量超过7500万册。福赛斯出生于1938年，曾任战斗机飞行员，后成为记者，在报道巴黎动荡和尼日利亚内战期间积累了大量素材。他于1969年创作《豺狼的日子》，讲述刺杀戴高乐的故事，获得巨大成功，并改编为电影。尽管福赛斯否认自己是间谍，但在自传中承认曾为MI6工作多年。他的作品常基于真实历史事件，如《敖德萨档案》涉及追捕纳粹战犯。福赛斯被授予CBE勋章和犯罪作家协会钻石匕首奖。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对作家Frederick Forsyth及其作品的评价与讨论

不同观点：

通过这些评论可以看出，Forsyth的作品在技术和情节描写上得到了广泛的认可，但其个人政治立场和作品中的某些价值观可能引发争议。

Frederick Forsyth
Frederick Forsyth, Day of the Jackal author and former MI6 agent, dies aged 86
Writer used his experience reporting on De Gaulle’s France to plot his thriller, and continued to draw on real-world research for subsequent bestsellers
Richard Lea
Mon 9 Jun 2025 12.42 EDT
Last modified on Mon 9 Jun 2025 12.53 EDT
Share
Frederick Forsyth, the author who turned his adventures as a journalist and work with MI6 into bestselling thrillers, has died after a brief illness aged 86.
Forsyth brought a reporter’s eye to his fiction, transforming the thriller genre with a series of novels including The Day of the Jackal, The Odessa File and The Dogs of War. Combining meticulous research with firecracker plots, he published a series of novels that sold more than 75m copies around the world, and won him honours including a CBE in 1997 and the Crime Writers’ Association Diamond Dagger award.
Born in Ashford, Kent in 1938, Forsyth flew fighter jets during his national service, but when the Royal Air Force couldn’t guarantee he’d stay in the cockpit he set out to see the world. While working for Reuters as a journalist, he got a lucky break. “The guy stationed in Paris got a heart murmur and had to come home,”
he told the Big Issue
. “A man stuck his head around the door of my office and said, ‘Anyone here speak French?’ Within days I was on the plane to Paris.”
Paris in 1961 was in turmoil, with rightwing militants threatening to assassinate Charles de Gaulle after his offer of independence to Algeria. “We were all waiting for the mega-story,”
the author recalled in the Express
, “the moment when a sniper got him through the forehead.” Forsyth got the inside track on the security operation from De Gaulle’s bodyguards and when a friend asked if an assassination would be successful, the writer shook his head. “It could be done,” Forsyth replied, “but only by an outsider. An assassin with no name, no face, no record, no dossier. And a professional.” The seed of an international bestseller was sown.
After spending time in East Germany, Forsyth moved to the BBC and in 1967 he was sent to Nigeria to cover the Biafran war. He arrived in the newly independent eastern region three days after the federal government’s invasion, having been told that the army would suppress the rebellion in a couple of weeks.
“My brief was to report the all-conquering march of the Nigerian army,”
Forsyth recalled
. “It did not happen. Naively, I filed this. When my report was broadcast our high commissioner complained to the CRO in London, who passed it on to the BBC – which accused me of pro-rebel bias and recalled me to London.”
Despairing of the BBC’s reluctance to challenge the British government’s support of the Nigerian regime, Forsyth quit and returned to Biafra as a freelance reporter in 1968. There he helped to break the story of the famine which shocked the world, and began working for MI6. Although Forsyth always denied he was a spy, in his 2015 autobiography, The Outsider,
the author admitted
he was an intelligence “asset” for more than 20 years. “There was nothing weird about it,”
he told a Guardian Live audience
, “it was the cold war. An awful lot of the strength of British intelligence came from the number of volunteers. A businessman might be going to a trade fair in a difficult-to-enter city and he’d be approached, quite gently, with a courteous, ‘If you would be so kind as to accept an envelope under your hotel door and bring it home …’ so that was what I did. I ran errands.”
Forsyth returned to the UK as the war came to an end in December 1969, finding himself with “no job, no prospects, no flat, no car, no savings”. Desperate to make money, he “hit on the most no-hope-in-hell way of making some:
write a novel
. I just sat down and wrote about the invisible assassin with no name. I knew my material; I had walked every inch of it. I wrote night and day for 35 days.”
The Day of the Jackal returned to Forsyth’s days in Paris, following an investigation to foil an assassin’s plot to kill De Gaulle. Packed full of operational details and putting fictional characters cheek by jowl with public figures, the novel brought a new realism to the thriller genre. The Guardian hailed it in 1971 as a “chilling, superbly researched story”, asking “Or is it fiction?” It rapidly became a word-of-mouth hit and a global bestseller, with a film adaptation released two years later.
In 1972’s The Odessa File, a young German reporter goes in search of the Nazi war criminal Eduard Roschmann and stumbles on an organisation defending high-ranking members of the SS.
The New York Times was scathing

data.title: Prince's special custom-font symbol floppy disks (2016)
data.author: arbesman
data.article_summary: 1993年，普林斯（Prince）将名字改为无法发音和打字的符号"The Love Symbol"，以抗议其唱片公司华纳兄弟（Warner Bros.）。这个改变不仅让唱片公司头疼，也给媒体和粉丝带来了困扰。为了解决无法打印其新名字的问题，普林斯设计了一种特殊字体，将符号替代字母P，并通过软盘分发给新闻机构。此举展示了普林斯对新兴技术的敏锐把握，尽管他后来对流媒体技术持怀疑态度。普林斯的团队成员回忆，他当时对消费者技术非常感兴趣，并积极参与图形和软件实验。这一创意举动成功让主流音乐刊物采用了自定义字体，显示了普林斯在艺术表达上的前瞻性。

主要讨论点：Prince更改名字和符号的行为及其影响和原因

不同观点：
• [frmersdog] 认为Prince改名与历史上其他人改名的现象有相似之处，例如Malcolm Little和FM-2030等人，都是为了消除与过去身份相关的痕迹。同时，他还提到在黑客、早期网络以及某些亚文化群体中也存在类似的匿名和改名现象，作为创造新身份或掩盖身份的手段。

• [bombcar] 强调Prince改名成功的原因不仅在于他的名气，还在于当时技术世界的全新状态以及他是第一个这样做的人。他认为如果所有人都这么做，这种行为将失去影响力，或者会促使统一的技术标准（如Unicode）的出现。同时，提到Prince最终还是恢复了原名。

• [dylan604] 引用了一个幽默的观点，指出Prince改名后要求大家使用新符号称呼他，而这种要求被广泛接受显得很滑稽。该评论进一步澄清了改名后的Prince不再希望被叫作“Prince”，这正是讨论的核心。

补充讨论：
• [badlibrarian] 提出一个假设性的幽默评论，设想如果Prince创建一个约会网站会怎样，这与讨论主题关系不大，但增加了对话的趣味性。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于Prince改名行为的独特性及其成功原因。一部分人认为这与他的名气和时代背景有关，而另一部分人关注的是这种行为在不同文化和群体中的普遍性及其背后的动机。

• 另一个小争议点是关于称呼Prince为“Prince”的问题，[dylan604]指出这种称呼实际上违背了Prince改名的初衷，而其他人可能没有意识到这一点。

总结来看，评论主要围绕Prince改名行为的背景、成功原因及其在不同文化和群体中的类似现象展开，同时带有一些幽默和假设性的讨论。

44192883.article_content:
In 1993, Prince frustrated contract lawyers and computer users everywhere when he changed his name to glyph known as “The Love Symbol.” Though he never said so explicitly, it’s generally understood that the name change was attempt to stick it to his record label, Warner Bros., which now had to deal with a top-tier artist with a new, unpronounceable, untypeable name. But it wasn’t just Warner Bros. that had a problem: The Love Symbol proved frustrating for people who wanted to both speak and write about Prince. Writers, editors, and layout designers at magazines and newspapers wouldn’t be able to type the actual name of the Artist Formerly Known As Prince. So Prince did the only thing you could do in that situation: He had a custom-designed font distributed to news outlets on a floppy
disk.
Here’s the floppy disk, from the collection of Anil Dash,
who’s written about it here
:
Added to my collection: 3.5" floppy given to press when Prince changed his name. Contains a font w/ one symbol in it.
pic.twitter.com/mNL0eOHDGI
— ଅନୀଲ (@anildash)
June 23, 2014
The Prince font substituted his symbol for what would otherwise be a capital P. In addition, the font was also made available for download on CompuServe. It was accompanied by a stern letter featuring both usage and installation instructions. (Graphix Zone, the company on the letterhead, released an interactive
CD
-
ROM
called
Prince Interactive
that same
year.)
For those asking, Prince font floppy is just a fun artifact; contents were on his CD-ROM & Compuserve 20 years ago.
pic.twitter.com/Mnzrvo64wQ
— ଅନୀଲ (@anildash)
June 23, 2014
The font idea, according to Chuck Hermes, who worked on the Paisley Park graphic-design team, came out of internal frustration. “
It just seemed like a logical thing to do,” Hermes told me over the phone today. “Everybody was having a hard time. He didn’t even want us to be calling him Prince in person. Part of it was, there was this glyph, this symbol that we didn’t know how to pronounce, and he wasn’t giving us any clues.
”
“
So we had to start communicating, we were just writing the symbol freehand,” he said. “It started out as we just did it for ourselves. We needed some way to be efficiently communicating with this name that we couldn’t type on a
keyboard.”
Steve Parke, who worked with Prince at the time, helped mail out the floppy disks. “He basically wanted people to start using that for his name in journalism,” Parke recalled, “and — I gotta be honest with you — I was like, ‘huh.’ I just remember when started I looking at those things I was like, ‘Really? I wonder how that’s gonna play
out.’”
It worked out pretty well. “I just remember maybe six months later,” Parke noted, “looking through
Rolling Stone
one time and seeing that symbol and I’m like, ‘Wow, that’s pretty impressive.’” After all, could any other artist convince a major music publication to integrate a custom
font?
“
How many people can just say ‘Hey, I’m changing my name to this symbol so can you use it from now on?’ and everyone’s like ‘Alright. Okay. No questions asked. You’re Prince! We’ll do it!’ It was kind of funny to
me.”
The move, catering to emerging technology in media, stands in contrast to Prince’s current reputation as a streaming-skeptical luddite and prolific issuer of takedown notices for his music on
YouTube.
“
I think he was very forward-thinking,” Parke remembered. “I think what happened a lot of time for him — not to be funny — he had an idea and the truth of the matter is the technology wasn’t quite there for what he
wanted.”
Hermes said that Prince, in the early ‘90s, was excited by consumer technology. “
I was working there and was kind of the first one to introduce him to bulletin-board systems and very early America Online back then. He was really engaged in all of this. We would spend hours every night. He’d come in and out of the studio and come into our offices just to experiment with graphics and Photoshop and all that software.” Unsurprisingly, Prince was thrilled at the possibility of being able to create art at such a rapid
clip.
But there were parts of the computer revolution that were still foreign to him. At least, until they were put in Prince’s own terms. “
I was talking about chat groups and chatting and meeting people online and he seemed confused by it,” Hermes reminisced. “Until I had told him I had met a girl. And that’s when he was able to go ‘Oh, I get it! I see where this could be useful.’
”

44192883.article_summary: 1993年，普林斯（Prince）将名字改为无法发音和打字的符号"The Love Symbol"，以抗议其唱片公司华纳兄弟（Warner Bros.）。这个改变不仅让唱片公司头疼，也给媒体和粉丝带来了困扰。为了解决无法打印其新名字的问题，普林斯设计了一种特殊字体，将符号替代字母P，并通过软盘分发给新闻机构。此举展示了普林斯对新兴技术的敏锐把握，尽管他后来对流媒体技术持怀疑态度。普林斯的团队成员回忆，他当时对消费者技术非常感兴趣，并积极参与图形和软件实验。这一创意举动成功让主流音乐刊物采用了自定义字体，显示了普林斯在艺术表达上的前瞻性。

data.title: Anthropic's AI-generated blog dies an early death
data.author: Sourabhsss1
data.article_summary: Anthropic近日推出了由其Claude AI模型撰写博客内容的"Claude Explains"博客，旨在结合客户需求和市场目标。然而，该博客在一周后被关闭，页面重定向至Anthropic主页，博客内容也已被删除。该博客最初作为展示Claude写作能力的平台，但由于未明确标注AI生成内容的比例，以及被质疑为自动化内容营销，社交媒体反响不佳。Anthropic可能因担忧AI生成内容的准确性和潜在错误而迅速停止了该项目。此前，其他媒体也曾因类似问题遭遇尴尬错误。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容在网络上的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• [anon7000] 认为AI生成网络内容是适得其反的，因为AI生成的内容并没有引入新的信息，只是重复模型中已有的内容。此外，过多的低质量生成内容可能会导致高质量信息的稀缺。
• [paxys] 对大型AI公司通过雇佣开发人员和内容创作者来烧钱的方式表示质疑，认为这种做法往往在短期内就被放弃，浪费资源。
• [pscanf] 调侃AI和人类在博客写作中的角色互换，AI被用来写博客但被当作人类创作，而AI公司却用人类写博客并当作AI生成内容。
• [joegibbs] 指出AI写作的问题在于它无法自动获取特定业务的最新信息，需要人为提供详细数据，导致生成内容要么是空洞的，要么需要花费大量时间调整提示词。
• [jasonthorsness] 关心是否有内容存档，并质疑一些博客下架原因的讨论，认为最终应关注内容质量本身。
• [Powdering7082] 询问是否有记者联系AI公司获取官方评论，质疑消息来源的可靠性。
• [jsnider3] 认为尝试新事物有时会失败，对AI写作的失败表示理解。
• [jsemrau] 观察到LinkedIn上AI生成内容的质量变化，从最初的改进到现在充斥着低质量的AI内容，指出问题在于创作者没有给出明确的风格指导。
• [neya] 反驳反对AI写作的人，指出AI生成内容的质量已经大幅提高，通过实验证明即使是专业编辑也难以区分AI和人类写作的区别，认为AI已经广泛应用于许多网站且难以察觉。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的质量及其对信息生态的影响，一部分人担心低质量内容泛滥，另一部分人则认为AI技术已经进步到难以区分人类和AI写作的程度。
• 对AI生成内容的态度存在分歧，一些人持怀疑态度，认为AI写作缺乏灵魂和创新，而另一些人则认为AI技术已经足够先进，能够替代人类写作。
• 讨论中还涉及AI生成内容的商业模式和资源消耗问题，质疑大型AI公司烧钱行为的效果和可持续性。

44225450.article_content:
Claude’s blog is no more.
A week after TechCrunch
profiled Anthropic’s experiment
to task the company’s Claude AI models with writing blog posts, Anthropic wound down the blog and redirected the address to its homepage. Sometime over the weekend, the Claude Explains blog disappeared — along with its initial few posts.
A source familiar tells TechCrunch the blog was a “pilot” meant to help Anthropic’s team combine customer requests for explainer-type “tips and tricks” content with marketing goals.
Claude Explains
, which had a dedicated page on Anthropic’s website and was edited for accuracy by humans, was populated by posts on technical topics related to various Claude use cases (e.g. “Simplify complex codebases with Claude”).  The blog, which was intended to be a showcase of sorts for Claude’s writing abilities, wasn’t clear about how much of Claude’s raw writing was making its way into each post.
An Anthropic spokesperson previously told TechCrunch that the blog was overseen by “subject matter experts and editorial teams” who “enhance[d]” Claude’s drafts with “insights, practical examples, and […] contextual knowledge.” The spokesperson also said Claude Explains would expand to topics ranging from creative writing to data analysis to business strategy.
Apparently, those plans changed in pretty short order.
“[Claude Explains is a] demonstration of how human expertise and AI capabilities can work together,” the spokesperson told TechCrunch earlier this month. “[The blog] is an early example of how teams can use AI to augment their work and provide greater value to their users. Rather than replacing human expertise, we’re showing how AI can amplify what subject matter experts can accomplish.”

Claude Explains didn’t get the rosiest reception on social media, in part due to the
lack of transparency
about which copy was AI-generated. Some users pointed out it looked a lot like an attempt to
automate content marketing
, an ad tactic that relies on generating content on popular topics to serve as a funnel for potential customers.
More than 24 websites were linking to Claude Explains posts before Anthropic wound down the pilot,
according
to search engine optimization tool Ahrefs. That’s not bad for a blog that was only live for around a month.
Anthropic might’ve also grown wary of implying Claude performs better at writing tasks than is actually the case. Even the best AI today is prone to confidently making things up, which has led to embarrassing gaffes on the part of publishers that have publicly embraced the tech. For example, Bloomberg has had to
correct dozens
of AI-generated summaries of its articles, and G/O Media’s error-riddled AI-written features — published against editors’ wishes —
attracted widespread ridicule
.

data.title: Trusting your own judgement on 'AI' is a risk
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了依赖自身判断面对人工智能（AI）相关决策的风险。作者以自己青少年时读过的Robert Cialdini的《影响力：说服的心理》一书为例，指出即使聪明人也很容易被操纵和误导，因为人类思维有固有局限。Cialdini的书揭示了人们如何被销售人员、骗子等利用认知漏洞进行操控，而这种操控往往绕过逻辑思考。作者强调，面对这些心理或认知风险，唯一的防御方法是避免被卷入其中，而非依赖智力或意志力。

文章进一步提到，软件开发人员特别容易受到这些风险影响，因为他们常常过于自信自己的判断。作者引用了一位CloudFlare工程师使用AI代理构建身份验证库的实验，指出这种单一个例并不能作为可靠证据，而更像是传闻。在软件开发中，基于传闻的讨论往往缺乏严谨的结构化研究支持，因此在处理具有重大影响的技术决策时，需格外谨慎。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于LLM（大型语言模型）和AI在软件开发中的应用及其争议

不同观点：
• flatline认为文章对TypeScript的批评是不正确且无根据的，指出静态类型检查在提高生产力和代码正确性方面的研究已有 decades 的历史，这种无端指责削弱了文章的说服力。
• lumenwrites批评作者在分析他人时忽视了自己的偏见，暗示作者可能存在双重标准。
• bigbadfeline强调AI的风险和副作用已经显现，特别是在社交媒体评论区中，但完全停止世界运转来研究AI不切实际。作者认为应在动态中研究AI，而不是提出不合理的要求来阻碍研究。
• tengbretson用挖地基的类比质疑文章的论点，认为作者的观点缺乏实际经验支持。
• croes指出人们从“不让FAANG（大科技公司）获取你的数据”到“把所有代码和数据交给AI”的转变非常讽刺，质疑对AI的信任。
• simonw认为文章开头对人类思维局限性的讨论实际上适用于作者自己，作者反对LLM的立场可能正是被自己描述的认知偏差所影响，建议重新审视自己的观点。
• fungiblecog认为对LLM的看法取决于对当前软件开发实践的看法，如果认为当前代码质量低劣，那么LLM生成的代码会被视为垃圾，反之亦然。
• lolc质疑代码审查的有效性，认为在LLM出现之前人们就在讨论代码质量问题，LLM只是放大了这些问题。
• colonCapitalDee表示不会等待科学研究来判断AI是否有用，倾向于通过自身使用和他人意见来形成观点，批评作者对Cloudflare实验的贬低是不合理的。

44225988.article_content:
Trusting your own judgement on 'AI' is a huge risk
9 June 2025
–
Baldur
Bjarnason
(This is loosely based on a couple of social media threads I posted last week, made longer and more tedious with added detail.)
One of the major turning points in my life was reading my dad’s copy of
Robert Cialdini’s
Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion
as a teenager.
Other highlights of my dad’s library – he was a organisational psychologist before he retired – included books by
Fanon
,
Illich
, and
Goffman
and a bunch on
systems thinking and systems theory
so, in hindsight, I was probably never
not
going to be idiosyncratic.
But Cialdini’s book was a turning point because it highlighted the very real limitations to human reasoning. No matter how smart you were, the mechanisms of your thinkings could easily be tricked in ways that completely bypassed your logical thinking and could insert ideas and trigger decisions that were not in your best interest.
He documented tactics and processes used by salespeople, thieves, and con artists and showed how they could manipulate and trick even smart people.
Worse yet, reading through another set of books in my dad’s library – those written by
Oliver Sacks
– indicated that the complex systems of the brain, the ones that lend themselves to manipulation and disorder, are a big part of what makes us human.
But to a self-important asshole teenager, one with an inflated sense of his own intelligence, Cialdini’s book was a timely deflation as it was specifically written as a warning to people to be careful about manipulation.
He described it as a process where the mechanics of cognitive optimisation in the brain could be deceptively triggered into a semi-automatic sequence that bypassed your regular judgement – his very eighties metaphor was like that of a tape in your mind that went “click whirr” and played in response to specific stimuli.
These are what I tend to call psychological or cognitive hazards. Like the golfer’s sand trap, the only way to win is to avoid them entirely.
Intelligence is not a defence. Most of these mechanisms and situations
feel
reasonable and intelligent in the moment.
Willpower, under these circumstances, is a myth. You can’t “will” your way to resisting these tactics. The only defence is avoidance.
What made me especially receptive to this idea at the time was the recent experience of having been sold a shitty CD player – that was obviously a sub-par model – by an excellent salesman.
“I’m smart. I’m a nerd who knows electronics. Why did I fall for these tricks?”
Because we all do is why.
Of course Cialdini later went on to focus more on teaching people how to
use
manipulative tactics to convince and sell, but his later lapse of ethical judgement doesn’t disprove the value of his groundbreaking initial book.
The reason why I’m outlining just how weird I was as a teenager and a young man is that software developers in particular are prone to being convinced by these hazards and few in the field seem to have ever had that “oh my, I can’t always trust my own judgement and reasoning” moment that I had.
A recent example was an experiment by a CloudFlare engineer at using an “AI agent”
to build an auth library from scratch.
From the project repository page:
I was an AI skeptic. I thought LLMs were glorified Markov chain generators that didn’t actually understand code and couldn’t produce anything novel. I started this project on a lark, fully expecting the AI to produce terrible code for me to laugh at. And then, uh… the code actually looked pretty good. Not perfect, but I just told the AI to fix things, and it did. I was shocked.
(If you don’t know what I mean with “an auth library” just know that it’s
the
most security sensitive and attacked point of any given web service. The consequences of a security flaw in this kind of library are potentially huge.)
Self-experimentation is gossip, not evidence
#
The debate surrounding this has been fairly typical for software development. The authors claimed that an Large Language Model (LLM) agent let them build it faster and more reliably than otherwise, many in software dev are convinced that this is powerful evidence that these tools really work.
It’s not, for a good reason, but it’s also important to note the process here that bypasses the judgement of even smart people.
First off, that project is a single person acting without any control. It has the evidentiary value of a blog post claiming that echinacea cured their cold complete with bloodwork showing no cold virus. That neither proves or disproves the value of echinacea. It’s just gossip.
When all you have is gossip (software development research is not great as it’s genuinely a separate problem domain from computer science) you have to make do with it – the debate about types, TypeScript, and web development is, for example, largely anecdotal gossip not backed by much in terms of structured research – but when you’re trying to answer a question with huge ramificatio
44225988.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了依赖自身判断面对人工智能（AI）相关决策的风险。作者以自己青少年时读过的Robert Cialdini的《影响力：说服的心理》一书为例，指出即使聪明人也很容易被操纵和误导，因为人类思维有固有局限。Cialdini的书揭示了人们如何被销售人员、骗子等利用认知漏洞进行操控，而这种操控往往绕过逻辑思考。作者强调，面对这些心理或认知风险，唯一的防御方法是避免被卷入其中，而非依赖智力或意志力。

文章进一步提到，软件开发人员特别容易受到这些风险影响，因为他们常常过于自信自己的判断。作者引用了一位CloudFlare工程师使用AI代理构建身份验证库的实验，指出这种单一个例并不能作为可靠证据，而更像是传闻。在软件开发中，基于传闻的讨论往往缺乏严谨的结构化研究支持，因此在处理具有重大影响的技术决策时，需格外谨慎。

Imagine that you have a song file—drums, guitar, bass, vocals, piano—and you want to rebalance it, bringing the voice down just a touch in the mix.
Or you want to turn a Lyle Lovett country-rock jam into a slamming club banger, and all that's standing between you and the booty-shaking masses is a clean copy of Lovett's voice without all those instruments mucking things up.
Or you recorded a once-in-a-lifetime, Stevie Nicks-meets-Ann Wilson vocal performance into your voice notes app... but your dog was baying in the background, and your guitar was out of tune. Can you extract the magic and discard the rest?
Without access to the original recording project files or master tapes, jobs like these have always been slightly difficult. Specialized tools or software could extract specific sounds, often the vocals, sometimes through crude techniques based around high- and low-passing the audio, but the results were never quite what one might wish. With the advent of machine learning, however, computers have gotten scarily good at reaching into dense audio mixes and surgically extracting complicated parts.
Apple's May 28 update to its flagship audio program, Logic Pro, shows just how far this tech has come—and how quickly it's advancing.
Put to the test
In 2024, Apple rolled out the Stem Splitter feature in Logic 11. Powered by AI tools and requiring Apple Silicon in order to work, Stem Splitter could "recover moments of inspiration from any audio file and separate nearly any mixed audio recording into four distinct parts: Drums, Bass, Vocals, and Other instruments, right on the device," Apple
said
. "With these tracks separated, it’s easy to apply effects, add new parts, or change the mix."
The original Stem Splitter in Logic.
And it worked—but it worked best as long as you kept all the stems together (that is, if you simply rebalanced the track or added effects to one of the stems). But if you wanted to
isolate
a single stem, you had to contend with some fairly gnarly audio artifacts.
Consider an example from a song I've been working on. Here's a snippet of the full piece:
After running Logic's original Stem Splitter on the snippet, I was given four tracks: Vocals, Drums, Bass, and "Other." They all isolated their parts reasonably well, but check out the static and artifacting when you isolate the bass track:
The vocal track came out better, but it was still far from ideal:
Now, just over a year later, Apple has released a point update for Logic that
delivers "enhanced audio fidelity"
for Stem Splitter—along with support for new stems for guitar and piano.
Logic now splits audio into more stems.
The difference in quality is significant, as you can hear in the new bass track:
And the new vocal track, though still lacking the pristine fidelity of the original recording, is nevertheless greatly improved:
The ability to separate out guitars and pianos is also welcome, and it works well. Here's the piano part:
Pretty impressive leap in fidelity for a point release!
There are plenty of other stem-splitting tools, of course, and many have had a head start on Apple. With its new release, however, Apple has certainly closed the gap.
Izotope's RX 11, for instance, is a highly regarded (and expensive!) piece of software that can do wonders when it comes to repairing audio and reducing clicks, background noise, and sibilance.
RX11, ready to split some stems.
It includes a stem-splitting feature that can produce four outputs (vocal, bass, drums, and other), and it produces usable audio—but I'm not sure I'd rank its output more highly than Logic's. Compare for yourself on the vocal and bass stems:
In any event, the AI/machine learning revolution has certainly arrived in the music world, and the rapid quality increase in stem-splitting tools in just a few years shows just what these AI systems are capable of when trained on enough data. I remain especially impressed by how the best stem splitters can extract not just a clean vocal but also the reverb/delay tail. Having access to the original recordings will always be better—but stem-splitting tech is improving quickly.
Nate Anderson

Deputy Editor
Nate is the deputy editor at Ars Technica. His most recent book is
In Emergency, Break Glass: What Nietzsche Can Teach Us About Joyful Living in a Tech-Saturated World
, which is much funnier than it sounds.

Celebrating 50K users with Kagi free search portal, Kagi for libraries, and more...
09 Jun, 2025
Just last week, we celebrated three years since Kagi was launched. We shared our
vision and roadmap
with you and this week, we are already at the next milestone - Kagi reaching 50,000 members!
We reached this milestone faster than the
previous one
, more than doubling our members since January 2024. We’re proud and grateful for your growing support. It helps us deliver on our shared mission.
Here’s a small sample of the countless supportive messages from our social media and community channels:
50k may seem small to some, but to us, each of you represents a conscious choice to reject the ad-tech and surveillance business model. Together, we’re exploring a different path to how the web should be experienced, one that resists a web controlled by advertising, SEO slop and manipulative algorithms. Our true measure isn’t in user statistics but in creating meaningful change that may benefit those who come after us.
The impact of our growth since the last milestone is visible in many ways:
Our community now includes 50,000 members, including over 5,000 families and nearly 200 teams
We’re approaching 1 million daily search queries
Orion browser has surpassed 1 million downloads
Our Discord community has grown to over 7,400 members
Thanks to your support, our team has expanded to about 40 people, enabling us to deliver more: improvements to Kagi Search, Wolfram Alpha integration, the launch of Kagi Assistant, our Android app and upcoming iOS app, Kagi Translate, progress towards Kagi Mail, upgrades to Kagi Maps and the development of Orion for Linux.
In keeping with our tradition of celebrating member milestones, we have several exciting announcements to share!
1. Announcing the free Kagi Search portal
We’re introducing several new products and initiatives designed to make Kagi more accessible, including a free Kagi Search portal.
In the coming days, we’ll roll out free access to Kagi Search for everyone. This means
anyone can experience Kagi Search without signing up, with 50 free searches directly from our homepage and 100 more after creating an account.
This will make it incredibly easy for anyone to try Kagi. You’ll be able to quickly share Kagi with a single link and instantly show others why you’re such a fan.
As an added bonus, you’ll also be able to share your Kagi search result pages freely with anyone.
Just copy the URL from your browser and share.
The free search portal ensures everyone can view your shared results, whether they’re Kagi members or not.
Note: the Kagi Search portal will be rolled out in phases, per region. We expect the full rollout to be completed within two weeks from now.
2. Announcing Kagi for Libraries
We often get inquiries from students and people who cannot afford Kagi about making Kagi more accessible. This was a difficult problem to solve and one we cared about a lot. At the heart of Kagi is public benefit and when libraries all over the world started contacting us about access to Kagi, we had an idea.
With Kagi for Libraries program, we will offer free access to Kagi for  public library patrons world-wide.
You will be able to simply visit a local library and enjoy free access to Kagi for all participating libraries.
Kagi for Libraries is a program designed to support public and academic libraries by offering a web search experience that upholds patron privacy and emphasizes reliable, verifiable information.
Libraries are pillars of knowledge, serving as equalizers, cultural preservers, and gateways to opportunity, particularly in communities where access to information, technology, and education is limited. By offering Kagi Search for free, we aim to strengthen libraries as gateways to opportunity and knowledge.
Search engines have become the foundation of modern learning and discovery, much like libraries have been for centuries. We believe private, high-quality search is essential digital infrastructure, ensuring fair and open access to knowledge in todayâs world. Kagi Search will be offered to libraries for free for an initial 12 months, with the idea of extending access for a discounted, fixed fee.
If your library is interested or you know a local public library that could benefit, encourage them to apply and help us expand this opportunity.
Go to
Kagi for Libraries
.
3. Wag like a doggo - in Kagi socks!
New Kagi-branded socks + stickers will hit our swag store during the summer.
Weâll get them in batches and give them away for free (just pay for the shipment) on a first-come, first-served basis. At this point, we are looking to have 20,000 pairs made. Since we created an entire supply chain
last time
, we thought we should make the most of it.
This is just a representation; the final design might vary.
Want a bit more of Kagi to brighten up your screens? Grab these fun wallpapers we’ve created just for you:
kagi.com/assets
We also have Kagi stickers for our
Discord Community

data.author: fallat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者在同事Jace的启发下，尝试创建一个既是Makefile又是Markdown的 polyglot 文件的过程。文章详细描述了如何利用Makefile的注释和Markdown的标题都是以`#`开头的特点，以及如何通过寻找其他"无操作"（no-op）语法来实现同时兼容两种格式的文件。作者逐步解决了代码块、普通文本段落等格式在两种语法中的兼容问题，最终成功创建了一个同时具备可执行性和可读性的Makefile.md文件。尽管这个实验可能不具备很大的实用价值，但它展示了通过创造性思维来融合不同语法功能的可能性。

不同观点：

This is a short story of how my coworker Jace sniped me into creating a polyglot
Makefile-Markdown file.
Never have I seen an article step through the process of creating a polyglot
file. Most are small trivial examples, or glance over the difficulties you may
run into. While there are plenty noteworthy ployglot projects
1
in the wild,
this Makefile.md experiment appears to be a public first. The idea of making
Markdown executable or adding human-readable elements to Makefiles appears
to be questionably useful, as there are a few projects that have tried to achieve
this merger in more "full solution" ways already
2
3
4
!
I'm a simple person though, who desires simple, beautiful, synergistic solutions.
On Friday (this article is posted on a Sunday), trudging through the Playwright
mines (a test framework typically for web applications), my coworker Jace said
something that immediately triggered me to do what this article details:
As soon as I opened our project's Makefile, it became crystal clear just how
compatible Markdown
could be
with Makefiles, partially thanks to how Jace
wrote it:
Oh my god
, a Makefile comment looks just like a Markdown header!
To take advantage of GitHub rendering
README.md

symlinked
the
Makefile
as the
README.md
to see how it'd
render with zero changes.
Copy snippet

ln -s Makefile README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "let's go"
git push
The result is interesting! But not digestible.
The universe. demands. better.
We need to now take in and reflect why this works in the first place. What is
making this successfully work?
What are the fundamentals at play?
Let's start with the statements:
# INSTALL
is a comment in Makefile.
# INSTALL
is a header in Markdown.
A comment in a no-op in Makefile.
A header is styling in Markdown.
Thus
#
is essentially a "stylistic no-op", doing no meaningful computation in Makefile but styling the document as Markdown.
This idea is pivotal in discovering new "styled-execution syntaxes".
Because Makefiles do essential computational work, we must find other "no-op"
operations that allow us to "pull through" Markdown syntax elements without
affecting the intended Makefile instructions!
From here on, I would have Makefile and Markdown documentation open to look
for everything and anything that helped move us toward the goal of rendering
more Markdown styles without affecting the Makefile scripts.
The next styling I decided to do was, unintuitively, code-blocks, because
we had
ifdef
s in our Makefile that I couldn't imagine looking any better

(Not looking too bad already!)
Copy snippet
```sh :

#\
```
There is one issue with this: it always leaves a trailing
#\
. I was
happy though and left it at that. Code-blocks were particularly hard because
Markdown demanded that the 3 backticks stood alone on their own line, but
Makefile was not happy, always complaining about a missing separator, but we
cannot use a separator due to what we just said.
To get around this, we are lucky Makefile supports what I'm going to call
"line-folding", where
\
is used to collapse two lines. See where we're going
with this? We collapse a comment
#
and the 3 backticks with
\
to keep
Makefile happy while rendering the code-block.
Phew!
Another noteworthy, interesting addition, is the abuse of Makefile's separator
:
to start the code-block. In Makefile's eyes, we are defining a
no-op recipe
,
which reads "for the recipe
\
``sh`, do nothing". Perfect for us! In the
the Markdown rendering, it's completely hidden.
Hold on minute... Whaaa, thinking more about
:
leads us to discover another amazing
"stylistic no-op"! It is the
dual
of
#
!
#
ignores everything
after
the symbol in Makefile.
:
ignores everything
before
the symbol in Makefile (if no dependencies).
Ho boy. Now we're really cooking.

The mental model was proving itself effective. Then I tackled plain text

of the evening:
[](:)
.
It's kinda cute.
Without this combination, all my plain-text would have a colon
:
on the end.
Using Markdown links with no text, we could effectively hide this colon!
Running the Makefile though, it complains about
)
being a missing dependency.
No problem, we will make this a no-op recipe!
):
, done!
With that, we could define any number of useful "no-op" recipes at the bottom
of the Makefile that
supports our Markdown styling
.

不同观点：
• **支持存档链接的观点**：

• **质疑存档链接可靠性的观点**：

   - 例子：有用户提到，存档网站本身可能存在技术问题，导致存档的内容不准确或缺失。

   - 有人提出，存档行为可能涉及侵犯版权，尤其当存档的内容是受版权保护的材料时。

• 争议焦点在于存档链接的可靠性和合法性，以及对新闻内容真实性的基本关注。

data.article_summary: 本文主要讨论了Rust编程语言编译速度慢和反馈循环时间长的问题。作者作为Rust编译器性能工作组成员，强调Rust项目非常重视编译器性能，并通过多种方式不断改进，如每周筛选性能提升和回退、运行基准测试套件等。尽管编译速度在过去几年已有显著提升，但对许多开发者而言，编译时间仍是一个瓶颈，尤其相较于C++或Python等语言。文章进一步探讨了Rust编译速度是否能达到接近即时重建的目标，指出对于大型项目或高度优化构建，实现即时编译可能不现实，但在增量编译模式下显著提升速度是有可能的。作者承认问题依然存在，并表示Rust团队正积极寻求解决方案。

44225419.article_content:
Perhaps the most often repeated complaint about Rust is its slow feedback loop and long compilation times. I hear about it all the time; in Rust podcasts,
blog
posts
,
surveys
, conference talks or offline discussions. I also regularly complain about it, being a Rust user myself!
Recently, in addition to the usual compile times complaints, I also started noticing the following sentiments being expressed by frustrated Rust developers: “Why doesn’t the Rust Project
care more
about this pressing and known issue? Why don’t they
do something
about it?”. As a member of the
Rust compiler performance working group
, I take these questions very seriously, and I of course have some opinions on the topic. In this blog post, I would like to offer some thoughts that might serve as answers to these (and other similar) questions.
Disclaimer: all opinions expressed in this post
are mine only
and do not necessarily represent the broader views of the Rust Project (the diverse set of contributors and maintainers that contribute to the Rust toolchain).
Do we even care?
First, let me assure you - yes, we (as in, the Rust Project)
absolutely do care
about the performance of our beloved compiler, and we put in a lot of effort to improve it. We
triage
performance improvements and regressions each week. We run a comprehensive
benchmark suite
after every
merged
PR
. We enthusiatically welcome any performance improvements (unless they have complicated trade-offs, more on that later), and try to quickly revert (or fix) PRs that introduce performance regressions. Very smart people are continously working on finding bottlenecks and
speeding up the compiler
. And some significant improvements to make compilation faster by default are currently
in the works
.
And all this effort shows results; Rust build performance has improved quite a lot over the past few years! When we talk about the long-term trends, we usually show
this dashboard
, but I find it a bit dull, because it averages results of several benchmarks together and the benchmarks are quite short, so they start running into diminishing returns. Instead, I did a little experiment to show how did the build performance evolve on my favourite test subject,
hyperqueue
. I took its first commit (from March 2021
1
) and compiled it with a few different Rust compiler versions, with ~1 year increments between them
2
. I did this on a relatively modest laptop with 8 AMD cores running Linux. Here are the results:
rustc
version
Clean build [s]
Incremental rebuild [s]
Speedup (clean build)
1.61.0
(May 2022)
26.1s
~0.39
-
1.70.0
(June 2023)
20.2s
~0.37
1.29x
1.78.0
(May 2024)
17.0s
~0.30
1.53x
1.87.0
(May 2025)
14.7s
~0.26
1.77x
On this benchmark, the compiler is almost twice as fast than it was three years ago. Of course, this is just a single data point, in different cases the speedup will be larger or smaller, and it will likely be smaller in general on other platforms than x64 Linux, because we spend the most effort optimizing that specific target. But the fact remains that the performance of the compiler is continuously improving.
It’s still not
fast enough
though
Now, all that is nice, but it doesn’t change the fact that for many Rust developers, compilation performance is still a big bottleneck, and they could be much more productive if the feedback loop was an order of magnitude (or more) faster. To be fair, this will depend on who you ask, e.g. some C++ developers don’t mind Rust’s compilation times at all, as they are used to the same (or worse) build times, while Python programmers likely aren’t very impressed by Rust’s feedback loop speed. But it’s definitely not a stretch to say that for many users, Rust compilation just isn’t
fast enough
today, and that is a problem.
Before we examine that problem in more detail, I think that it’s interesting to think about whether the problem is even fundamentally solvable, and what is the end goal that we would eventually like to achieve. Can Rust ever hope to achieve near-instant (re)build speeds, with its complex type system, borrow checking, monomorphization, proc macros and build scripts, large translation units, machine code generation and a “rebuild the world from source” compilation model? When it has a historical track record of favoring runtime (rather than compilation) performance at
nearly every opportunity
?
I think that it depends on the use-case. If we’re talking about building projects with hundreds of dependencies from scratch or doing super-duper
LTO
-optimized release builds, I think that we won’t ever get to a point where the build will be truly
instant
. On the other hand, I personally believe (although others might disagree!) that it is not fundamentally impossible to have a Rust compiler that will be able to almost instantly rebuild a Rust project of nearly any size in incremental (and at least moderately optimized) mode after making a small change to the source code, one where rebuilds are truly

主要讨论点： bug报告的难度和有效性

不同观点：
• **mmsc**：认为开放式bug报告会带来大量无用或疯狂的反馈，导致有用的报告被淹没。建议设置两种报告方式：简单截图和详细报告，并提议使用LLM（大型语言模型）自动过滤无用报告。
• **D13Fd**：指出bug报告经常得不到修复回应，导致用户失去报告的动力。即使是一些容易修复的bug，也常常没有下文。
• **kelipso**：认为在移动应用中找到bug报告按钮并报告bug的过程不值得，因为报告很可能不会被查看。
• **wittjeff**：分享了自己为残疾用户开发的更易用的报告工具，结合了注释功能和W3C Web注释规范，并考虑记录用户操作以提供更准确的复现步骤。
• **cwillu**：指出bug报告是一个双向过程，如果提交后没有反馈，用户将失去报告的动力。
• **cosmotic**：提出企业可能有反向激励，不愿意简化bug报告流程，因为报告数量可能被视为软件质量的指标。
• **Oras**：建议使用工具如PostHog或Clarify来记录用户会话和错误日志，以替代用户手动报告。
• **graypegg**：喜欢UI设计概念，但担心“bug”这个词对普通用户有歧义，建议使用“issue”或“problem”等更明确的词。
• **LanceJones**：对bug报告工具的可见性和用户引导提出建议，并提议在报告中包含更多上下文信息如CSS类。
• **Rick76**：引用苹果的例子，强调简化操作对用户体验的重要性。
• **5040**：提到Kindle的错误报告功能，但质疑报告是否被处理。
• **OsrsNeedsf2P**：对比Google的“反馈”按钮，质疑当前设计选择的原因。
• **pxtail**：认为用户不应该为付费软件报告bug，因为这是QA团队的工作，用户不应该成为免费劳动力，除非获得折扣或其他补偿。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：用户是否应为付费软件报告bug，以及企业是否有动机简化bug报告流程。
• **重要论据**：简化报告流程和提供反馈对提高用户报告积极性的重要性，以及自动过滤和分类无用报告的技术可能性。
• **设计建议**：包括UI设计、引导提示、报告内容上下文的增强，以及为特殊用户群体（如残疾用户）提供更易用的报告工具。

不同观点：
• **mmsc**：认为开放式bug报告会带来大量无用或疯狂的反馈，导致有用的报告被淹没。建议设置两种报告方式：简单截图和详细报告，并提议使用LLM（大型语言模型）自动过滤无用报告。
• **D13Fd**：指出bug报告经常得不到修复回应，导致用户失去报告的动力。即使是一些容易修复的bug，也常常没有下文。
• **kelipso**：认为在移动应用中找到bug报告按钮并报告bug的过程不值得，因为报告很可能不会被查看。
• **wittjeff**：分享了自己为残疾用户开发的更易用的报告工具，结合了注释功能和W3C Web注释规范，并考虑记录用户操作以提供更准确的复现步骤。
• **cwillu**：指出bug报告是一个双向过程，如果提交后没有反馈，用户将失去报告的动力。
• **cosmotic**：提出企业可能有反向激励，不愿意简化bug报告流程，因为报告数量可能被视为软件质量的指标。
• **Oras**：建议使用工具如PostHog或Clarify来记录用户会话和错误日志，以替代用户手动报告。
• **graypegg**：喜欢UI设计概念，但担心“bug”这个词对普通用户有歧义，建议使用“issue”或“problem”等更明确的词。
• **LanceJones**：对bug报告工具的可见性和用户引导提出建议，并提议在报告中包含更多上下文信息如CSS类。
• **Rick76**：引用苹果的例子，强调简化操作对用户体验的重要性。
• **5040**：提到Kindle的错误报告功能，但质疑报告是否被处理。
• **OsrsNeedsf2P**：对比Google的“反馈”按钮，质疑当前设计选择的原因。
• **pxtail**：认为用户不应该为付费软件报告bug，因为这是QA团队的工作，用户不应该成为免费劳动力，除非获得折扣或其他补偿。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：用户是否应为付费软件报告bug，以及企业是否有动机简化bug报告流程。
• **重要论据**：简化报告流程和提供反馈对提高用户报告积极性的重要性，以及自动过滤和分类无用报告的技术可能性。
• **设计建议**：包括UI设计、引导提示、报告内容上下文的增强，以及为特殊用户群体（如残疾用户）提供更易用的报告工具。

data.title: Apple's New Design Language Is Liquid Glass
data.author: m463
data.article_summary: Apple在2025年WWDC上推出了全新的设计语言——Liquid Glass，将应用于iOS 26、iPadOS 26、macOS Tahoe 26等系统。Liquid Glass强调透明和玻璃光泽效果，融入应用界面，如锁屏、 dock和相机应用等，具备适应光暗环境的能力，并采用实时渲染技术。macOS Tahoe 26也大量使用该设计，包括透明菜单栏等。此设计是Apple自2013年放弃拟物设计后最重大的更新，将促使开发者调整应用。Apple还发布了新API供开发者适配。微软等公司也曾使用类似透明效果设计。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple新界面设计的独特性、视觉效果及其实际应用

不同观点：
• [9d] 对Apple声称的“只有Apple能实现的流畅性”表示怀疑，认为这种说法不实。他指出，其他开发者也能很快复制这种效果，并提到Material Design可能在一个月内就会采用类似的设计。他认为，这种排他性宣传在今天是站不住脚的。

• [mosdl] 认为Apple新设计的流动性效果过于分散注意力，可能在使用体验上并不理想。

• [bigyabai] 对设计的视觉对比和层次感提出看法，认为新设计缺乏以前拟物设计的高对比度。同时，他赞扬Material Design通过强调色来改善界面 cohesiveness（ cohesive：有凝聚力的），并指出Apple的设计虽然精良但不免显得过于 clinical（临床的，这里可能指过于简洁或冷淡）。他还对Dynamic Island和Control Center是否会被误认为应用控制而非系统控制表示担忧。

补充讨论：
• [bigyabai] 指出Apple的设计并非neumorphism（新拟物设计），但各层次界面分明，这可能会导致用户对界面元素的识别产生混淆。

争议焦点：
• Apple新设计是否真的具有独特性以及其视觉效果是否过于分散注意力。

News
Apple’s new design language is Liquid Glass
Liquid Glass is coming to iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, and more.
Liquid Glass is coming to iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, and more.
by
Tom Warren
Jun 9, 2025, 5:12 PM UTC
Link
Facebook
Threads
Image: Apple
Tom Warren
is a senior editor and author of
Notepad
, who has been covering all things Microsoft, PC, and tech for over 20 years.
Apple is introducing a new Liquid Glass design across its software platforms today. It’s all about adding transparency and glass shine effects to Apple’s in-app interfaces across its renamed
iOS 26
, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26 operating systems.
“[It’s] our broadest design update, ever,” says Alan Dye, Apple’s VP of human interface. “For the first time we’re introducing a universal design across our platforms.” The new design adds glass-like elements throughout iOS, including to the dock and the lockscreen, and it’s designed to mimic the optical qualities of glass.
A lot of glass-like effects and animations are coming to iOS 26.
Image: Apple
Liquid Glass is inspired by Apple’s visionOS software, and can adapt to light and dark environments. When you swipe up on the iOS 26 lock screen there’s a glass edge, and elements throughout the OS have glass edges to them. Even the camera app has the glass feel, with menus that are transparent and features that overlay on top of the camera feed.
Liquid Glass uses real-time rendering and will dynamically reacts to movement. Apple is using it on buttons, switches, sliders, text, media controls, and even lager surfaces like tab bars and sidebars. Apple has redesigned its controls, toolbars, and navigation within apps to fit this new Liquid Glass design.
macOS Tahoe 26 has lots of Liquid Glass elements, too.
Image: Apple
Apps like Camera, Photos, Safari, FaceTime, Apple Music, Apple News, and Apple Podcasts have all been updated for Liquid Glass. Apple is publishing an updated set of APIs to allow developers to start updating their apps, ahead of this new design update that’s launching later this year.
Apple is also using Liquid Glass in macOS Tahoe 26, with the dock, sidebars, and toolbars all getting a touch of the glass design. The menu bar is also now completely transparent in macOS Tahoe 26, a change that’s designed to make display feels bigger.
Apple’s shift away from skeuomorphism in iOS 7 in 2013 has left its mobile OS looking very similar for
more than 10 years
, with the iOS 7 design style still influencing the most recent versions of iOS. Liquid Glass looks a lot different, and it’s going to force app developers to really adjust their apps in the coming months.
Apple has also used glass themes in the past, most notably with the introduction of Aqua, which first appeared in iMovie 2 in 2000 before rolling out more broadly in Mac OS X 10.0 in 2001.
macOS 11 Big Sur also introduced
a big redesign to the macOS UI, with more rounded corners, greater use of transparent and translucent layers, and a slew of new icons.
Microsoft has also been using transparency effects in its Windows operating system since it launched Windows Vista in 2007, complete with its own Aero Glass theme. The current version of Windows 11 now uses Microsoft’s Fluent Design language, which increasingly has more of a focus on
3D, colorful, and playful
elements.

WWDC 2025 live blog
for all the latest news.

June 9, 2025
macOS Tahoe 26 makes the Mac more capable, productive, and intelligent than ever
Introducing a stunning new design, more Continuity experiences with the Phone app and Live Activities, the biggest update to Spotlight ever, and expanded Apple Intelligence capabilities
macOS Tahoe 26 introduces a beautiful new design, additional Continuity experiences, along with even more features to turbocharge productivity.
CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA
Apple today previewed the next major macOS release — macOS Tahoe 26 — which introduces a stunning new design and powerful capabilities that enable users to get even more done. With the new design, iconic elements of macOS will feel more expressive, delightful, and personal while remaining instantly familiar, including the desktop, Dock, in-app navigation, and toolbars. Users can further personalize the experience with an updated Control Center and new color options for folders, app icons, and widgets. Continuity gets even better with the Phone app arriving on Mac, so users can access familiar features from iPhone — including Recents, Contacts, and Voicemails — and new ones like Call Screening
1
and Hold Assist.
2
And with Live Activities from iPhone, users can stay on top of things happening in real time, like an upcoming flight, right on their Mac. Spotlight gets its biggest update ever, allowing users to now directly execute hundreds of actions — like sending an email or creating a note — and take advantage of all-new browsing experiences to get to content faster.
Apple Intelligence expands with powerful new features that elevate the Mac experience further, while protecting privacy at every step. Live Translation helps users easily communicate across languages, translating text and audio. Genmoji and Image Playground offer new options for creativity.
3
Shortcuts get even more powerful with intelligent actions and the ability to now tap directly into Apple Intelligence models to automate complex tasks.
“macOS is the heart and soul of the Mac, and with Tahoe, we’re building on what users love most. Whether you’re a power user or just getting started on Mac, there’s something for everyone, with even more features to turbocharge productivity and make working across Mac and iPhone more seamless than ever before,” said Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice president of Software Engineering. “With its gorgeous new design, amazing Continuity experiences, powerful enhancements to Spotlight, more intelligent shortcuts, and updates to Apple Intelligence, the Mac experience is better than ever.”
The new design unlocks even more ways to personalize the Mac.

A Gorgeous New Design
The gorgeous new design enhances the Mac experience in new ways, while maintaining the familiarity of macOS. It is crafted with Liquid Glass, a translucent new material that reflects and refracts its surroundings. The Dock, sidebars, and toolbars have been refined, bringing greater focus to a user’s content. The menu bar is now completely transparent, making the display feel even larger. There are more ways to customize what controls appear in the menu bar and Control Center, along with how they’re laid out. The new design also unlocks more personalization on the Mac. App icons come to life in light or dark appearances, colorful new light and dark tints, as well as an elegant new clear look. Users can also change the colors of folders and add a symbol or emoji to give them a unique identity. And when combined with personalized wallpapers and theme colors, it’s easier than ever to make Mac a seamless extension of a user’s style.
The new design elevates iconic elements of macOS, making them at once fresh and timelessly Mac. From the moment a user unlocks their Mac, the desktop is instantly familiar.
There are more ways to customize what controls appear in Control Center and the menu bar, along with how they’re laid out.
Sidebars and toolbars in apps are crafted from Liquid Glass, bringing more focus to users’ content and reflecting the depth of their workspace.

The Phone app arrives on Mac thanks to Continuity, which lets users relay cellular calls from their nearby iPhone. The Phone app on Mac has the familiar features of the Phone app on iPhone — including Recents, Favorites, and Voicemails — and the latest updates like Call Screening and Hold Assist. Call Screening automatically answers calls from unknown numbers and asks the caller for information so a user can decide whether or not to answer. And when a user is stuck on hold, Hold Assist allows them to keep their spot in line while they wait for a live agent, so users can continue working on their Mac.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI编码助手在编程工作中的使用及其影响

不同观点：
• **支持有限使用AI编码助手**：
  - fzwang：有限地允许初级开发人员使用AI助手，仅限于LLM擅长的任务，如验证性、重复性工作。早期生产力有所提升，但长期使用可能导致学习速度减慢和系统理解模糊。
  - sifuhotman2000：新工程师比老工程师更快接受AI，老工程师往往因为初期挫折而放弃AI，但AI可以提高生产力。

• **反对使用AI编码助手**：
  - toast0：倾向于传统方法，认为使用新工具未必更高效，传统方法虽然可能不高效，但稳定可靠。
  - vouaobrasil：坚决反对使用AI，认为手动编码是享受编程乐趣的一部分，AI强调效率而忽视了编程的创造性和乐趣。
  - soapdog：认为AI助手不道德且笨重，不愿意使用。

• **对AI编码助手持中立或条件接受态度**：
  - torham：周围大多数工程师尝试过LLM，但大多数仍不依赖它，自己在某些情况下会使用Gemini webapp，但成功率不高。
  - jeremy_k：仅在重构时使用AI，不需要AI的建议功能，因为自己已清楚目标和结果。
  - zy5a59：虽然AI提高了效率，但减少了编程乐趣，因此根据情况选择是否使用AI。
  - toldyouso2022：区分工作与娱乐编程，娱乐时不用AI，工作时可能会用。

• **对AI编码助手的具体问题和争议**：
  - rsyncnott：曾使用Copilot一周后因其频繁出错和分散注意力而关闭。
  - el_magnificus：认同使用LLM令人沮丧，但在无网络环境下纯手工编码感觉良好，认为未来会找到合理使用LLM的方法。

• **对AI影响编程哲学和技能的担忧**：
  - jurisjs：担心AI会破坏已有的设计哲学和问题解决方法，特别是经过多年实践形成的有效方法。

• **传统方法仍占主导地位**：
  - JohnFen：大多数开发人员仍以传统方式工作，或至少90%的工作依赖传统方法。

补充讨论：
- AI编码助手提高了短期生产力，但可能影响长期技能发展和系统理解。
- 编程的乐趣与创造性在AI使用中被忽视，部分程序员认为手动编码过程本身是一种享受。
- 对AI的接受程度存在代际差异，新一代工程师更愿意尝试AI工具。
- 对AI的伦理问题和自动化带来的潜在负面影响存在担忧，特别是对人类创造力和技能发展的影响。

• [indianmouse] 认为通过系统学习NVIDIA提供的指南和书籍，并结合实践项目，可以在6-8周内掌握CUDA编程。他强调需要具备较强的C语言基础，并推荐使用Github上的CUDA项目和LLM（大型语言模型）来辅助理解代码。
• [throwaway81523] 指出CUDA编程本身与C++类似，但如果目标是从事AI编程，需要深入学习AI相关知识。他还提到3D图形学也是一个复杂且深入的领域，初学者可能需要花费大量时间来掌握。
• [FilosofumRex] 认为如果目标是赚钱，应该专注于PTX、nvcc、cuobjdump、Nsight等工具的精通，而不是高性能计算（HPC）和数学相关的知识。他推荐加入Discord的gpumode社区以获取更多实际编程经验。
• [lokimedes] 将学习CUDA分为三个方面：学习CUDA框架和库、学习高性能计算方法、以及应用领域的特定知识。他强调高性能计算知识的可转移性，并建议从高层次抽象开始学习，再深入到基础知识。
• [elashri] 分享了个人学习CUDA的经验，强调学习过程中的试错和调试过程。他建议初学者不要一开始就关注优化，而是先确保代码正确，再逐步优化。

补充讨论：
• [imjonse] 提供了一些学习资源和社区链接，认为这些资源可以帮助学习者花费数月时间掌握CUDA。
• [mekpro] 提问关于哪些公司和职位需要CUDA工程师，认为虽然很多公司使用CUDA的衍生产品，但直接的CUDA开发职位可能较少。
• [SonOfLilit] 推荐从prefix scan入手学习GPU编程，并建议在掌握基础后尝试实现一些优化算法，如GEMM和FlashAttention。
• [alecco] 建议从CUDA Thrust开始学习，认为Thrust和cub可以解决80%的常见问题，并推荐在有一定经验后再深入学习cub。
• [canyp] 强调学习GPU硬件架构和并行算法的重要性，认为这些是CUDA开发职位所需的核心技能。
• [math_dandy] 询问是否有GPU模拟器可以在普通笔记本上运行简单的CUDA程序，以方便学习工具链和 mechanics。
• [fifilura] 将CUDA编程与Spark和SQL进行类比，建议初学者习惯不使用for循环的编程方式。

争议的焦点：
• 学习CUDA的最佳路径：有些人建议从NVIDIA的官方资源开始系统学习，而另一些人建议从实际项目和工具入手。
• CUDA在职业发展中的实际应用：有人认为直接的CUDA开发职位较少，而更多地是使用CUDA的衍生产品，如PyTorch。
• 优化的时机：有人建议初学者一开始不要过分关注优化，而应先确保代码正确，而另一些人则强调从一开始就关注性能问题。

总结：
讨论中提供了多种学习CUDA的路径和资源，涵盖了从官方指南、社区资源到实际项目和工具的使用。参与者还讨论了CUDA在职业发展中的应用和潜在职位，以及学习过程中的一些具体技巧和建议。

data.title: Feline Genetics and Why Orange Cats Are the Most Special
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 近期研究揭示了橙色猫咪毛色的遗传机制。科学家发现，橙色毛色是由X染色体上的突变引起的，该突变抑制了黑色素（eumelanin）的生成，促进了橙色素（pheomelanin）的表达。具体来说，一个与X染色体上ARHGAP36基因相关的5-5.1千碱基（kb）片段的缺失，增加了该基因的表达，从而抑制了黑色素的产生。约80%的橙色猫为雄性，因为雌性需要两条X染色体同时携带该突变才能表现为橙色。此外，研究还探讨了不同猫品种的毛发长度和图案的遗传基础，如FGF5基因决定毛发长度，而“虎斑”图案可能源于野猫。这些发现帮助理解了猫咪毛色和图案的多样性及其遗传背景。
